response.summary: The plan's structure is sound: pins come before moves, variant encoders are never merged, and there are rules for shims and source scans. But there are three problems with what it claims. First, RF0 is allowed to run now and rewrites public-launch's own authority ledger and the test that guards it. Second, the RF1 pins do not cover the checker, diff, safefs, assurance and synth behaviour that RF3, RF4 and RF6 change. Third, the RF-D2 gate stops at Phase 4 sign-off, but Phase 5 publication comes after it. Further hardening issues: the move-only commit rule conflicts with the monkeypatch rule, the budgets have no floor, audit numbers are hard-coded into criteria, some completion predicates cannot fail, and RF-D6 tightens behaviour inside a phase that is meant to preserve it.

evidence.observation: “Moves and merges preserve CLI/API names, schemas, exit codes, messages, refusals, deterministic output bytes and digests.”
“Rename the three `model_digest` functions to names that state what each one means.” RF2's criteria require unchanged behavior pins but do not require the old callable names to remain importable.

concerns.recommendation: Specify compatibility aliases for existing callable names and add import-path pins, or obtain an explicit compatibility decision for each removal.
concerns.title: RF2 renames digest functions without enforcing the promised API compatibility

evidence.observation: “No other audit claim was re-proved. RF0 re-measures all of them with a committed tool.”
“the 47 private imports from `synth.boundary` into `synth.mutate` are replaced by public oracle imports.”

concerns.recommendation: Label 47 as an unverified audit count and define RF4-C3 against the RF0-measured inventory, including how a different count changes the target.
concerns.title: RF4 fixes an acceptance target to an unverified audit count

response.summary: The plan needs an enforceable compatibility rule for renamed digest functions and must make one audit-derived RF4 target conditional on RF0 measurement.

evidence.observation: "Nothing in `src/gnd` changes until the plan gate, the RF0 handoff record, and the public-launch sign-offs that RF-D2 names." The RF0 handoff record is itself produced by RF0, so the gate conditions src/gnd edits on an artifact that RF0 creates.
"**RF0–RF1 do not edit `src/gnd`.**" and "Under RF-D2, RF0 and RF1 may run now." Section 8 states the plan gate has not happened yet: "The next step is plan review and the owner plan gate."

evidence.location: Section 4, RF0 body; Section 5 table, last row
evidence.observation: RF0 must "Record the unit handoff in `migration/units.json`, and update the test that currently requires every unit to be source-owned", and Section 5 assigns "`tests/test_public_distribution.py`, distribution manifest | Update procedure decided in RF-D3. | RF0". The plan never gives the repository-relative path of `migration/units.json` or the distribution manifest, and Section 2 shows other referenced records do live under `src/gnd` ("`src/gnd/skills/gnd-orm-core/references/milestone-record-format.md`").

concerns.recommendation: State the exact paths of `migration/units.json`, the units-ownership test and the distribution manifest, and record for each whether it is under `src/gnd`. If any is, either move that RF0 deliverable behind the RF-D2 sign-offs or record an explicit owner exemption, and rewrite the header sentence so the preconditions for a src/gnd edit are non-circular (plan gate plus RF-D2 sign-offs, with the RF0 handoff record named as an RF0 output rather than a precondition).
concerns.title: RF0's authorized-now scope contradicts the src/gnd edit gate it is supposed to satisfy

evidence.observation: "**Thin entry points:** `cli.py` is a dispatcher over `commands/<group>.py` modules, and no command handler holds domain logic that `api.py` or a lane `service.py` cannot also reach." No criterion in RF5 tests the second clause.

"RF5-C3 `cli.py` shrinks to at most the line budget the spec declares." The bound is chosen by the document that is being gated, and the plan sets no floor, no reduction ratio and no owner approval requirement for it, against a re-measured baseline of "`cli.py` 9,088".

"RF5-C1 the RF1 parser, help and exit pins are unchanged. RF5-C2 tests that require `gnd.cli` to stay unloaded also cover `gnd.commands.*`. RF5-C3 ... RF5-C4 every monkeypatch of a moved name targets the new location." None of the four instruments predicate 4's dispatcher/domain-logic claim.

concerns.recommendation: Give predicate 4 an instrument: an absolute plan-level ceiling or required reduction ratio for `cli.py` measured by the RF0 tool and approved at the owner gate, plus a named check for the domain-logic clause (a test asserting each moved handler's logic is reachable from `api.py` or a lane `service.py`, or a per-handler reachability table committed in the RF5 spec and reviewed at its gate).
concerns.title: Completion predicate 4 cannot be demonstrated: RF5-C3's budget is self-declared and the domain-logic clause has no criterion

evidence.observation: "every `monkeypatch` of a moved name is re-pointed at the new location in the same phase" and "Tests that scan source text (`inspect.getsource`, reads of `cli.py`, "module stays unloaded" checks) are widened to cover each new module in the same phase. A test asserts that the scanned set covers every module it is meant to cover."

evidence.observation: RF3 gates on "no SCC among the core modules", a private-import count and "every `semantic_registry` `owner=` string resolves to an existing function"; RF4 gates on "the `assurance`, `synth` and `api↔diff` SCCs are gone", "no lane imports `install`" and the 47 private imports. In each case the number that decides the gate is written by the phase being gated.

"A metric that gets worse without a recorded reason is a review finding." This forbids regression but does not require improvement, so a spec target equal to the RF0 baseline satisfies RF2-C2, RF3-C2 and RF6-C1 with no consolidation achieved.
"If so, the spec splits RF5 into numbered parts, each with its own record." Overrun handling exists for RF5 only; no phase states a stop condition for a target that proves unreachable mid-phase.

concerns.recommendation: Require in RF-R9 that every spec target be derived from the RF0 measurement, be strictly better than the RF0 baseline by a stated margin, and be approved at the owner spec gate; forbid a target equal to the baseline. Add a uniform stop condition: a phase whose measured target proves unreachable stops and returns to the owner gate rather than re-declaring the target.

response.summary: The plan is MVP-ordered, pins behavior before moves (RF-R3/RF1), separates move-only diffs (RF-R4), and defers tightening to RF7 under RF-D7. Two gates are not demonstrable as written: the src/gnd edit gate that authorizes RF0 now is circular and never states whether migration/units.json or the distribution manifest live under src/gnd, and completion predicate 4 (thin entry points) has no instrument because RF5-C3 defers its line budget to the spec and no criterion covers the domain-logic clause. Several further criteria are self-set (RF2-C2, RF3-C2, RF6-C1), scope-less (RF4-C2, RF1 layering test, RF8-C2 territory), keyed to audit numbers the plan says were not re-proved (RF4-C3), or omit phase obligations that RF-R5/RF-R6 make binding (monkeypatch re-pointing and source-scan widening outside RF5).

RF-R1 states: 'Moves and merges preserve CLI/API names, schemas, exit codes, messages, refusals, deterministic output bytes and digests. Any observable change needs its own decision row and owner ruling. Merely sitting in a refactor phase does not authorize it.' The decision table in section 10 (RF-D1..RF-D9) contains no row authorizing the model_digest renames, and RF-R5's shim inventory only guarantees that 'old import paths stay importable through re-exports' — module paths, not renamed symbols — so nothing requires `model_digest` and its siblings to remain importable after RF2. Completion predicate 1 (line 33) also requires pins to stay green 'unchanged except through recorded compatibility decisions', and no such recorded decision exists for the rename.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit decision row (or fold into an RF-D8-style ruling) authorizing the renames, and extend RF-R5 or RF2's criteria so each renamed function remains importable under its old name via a listed shim with a retirement trigger until RF-D5's retirement phase.
concerns.title: RF2 renames public model_digest API without a decision row or symbol-level shim

evidence.observation: RF4-C3 reads: 'the 47 private imports from `synth.boundary` into `synth.mutate` are replaced by public oracle imports.' The plan itself states at lines 15-16: 'No other audit claim was re-proved. RF0 re-measures all of them with a committed tool.' If RF0 refutes the audit's count of 47, the criterion as written cannot be satisfied (or could be vacuously gamed) because, unlike RF0-C1 ('reproduces at least the core 13-module SCC, or the record explains the difference'), RF4-C3 has no fallback binding it to the RF0 re-measured value.

concerns.recommendation: Reword RF4-C3 so the target count is the RF0-confirmed number of private `synth.boundary`→`synth.mutate` imports, with a recorded note if the audit's 47 is refuted, mirroring the escape hatch in RF0-C1.
concerns.title: RF4-C3 hard-codes the audit's unverified '47 private imports' as a pass/fail criterion

evidence.location: lines 232-233 (RF7 'Not executed in this milestone') vs line 313 (section 9 verification selection)
evidence.observation: RF7 states: 'Not executed in this milestone. The milestone close carries it as an open question naming the successor milestone.' Yet the verification-selection table lists RF7 as a row with the mandatory focused obligation 'Red-before-green per newly refused input' and starting points, the same format used for executable phases, and RF-D7's deferral is not referenced from that row.

concerns.recommendation: Mark the RF7 row in section 9 as deferred/not-executed (or drop it), so a reviewer at a later phase gate does not treat RF7 verification as a gating obligation of this milestone.
concerns.title: Deferred RF7 appears in the verification-selection table with a mandatory obligation

response.summary: Reviewed the code-refactoring milestone plan r1 against its rubric: pinning-before-move, digest-bound bytes, monkeypatch and source-scan coverage are all enforced by RF-R1..RF-R11 and per-phase criteria; sequencing, RF-D1/RF-D2/RF-D7 rulings, audit-claim caveats and stop conditions are consistently recorded. Three concerns: RF2 mandates renaming the three public model_digest functions with no decision row and no shim obligation for renamed symbols, contradicting RF-R1's own API-name preservation rule; RF4-C3 hard-codes the unverified audit count of 47 private imports as a criterion with no fallback to the RF0 re-measurement; and the deferred RF7 still appears in the verification-selection table with a mandatory obligation, contradicting its 'not executed in this milestone' status.

evidence.observation: RF1 claims 'current behavior is pinned at every surface later phases touch', but its enumerated pins cover only 'the parser tree, help text and exit-code map for each command', canonical-JSON variant bytes, 'the three model_digest meanings', the two divergent primitive resolvers, ISO-datetime sites and 'one golden replay per session-contract version'. RF4 nonetheless moves the safe-filesystem functions public, splits agent_cli, makes the synth oracle public and repackages the assurance modules, and RF6 splits model.py and checker.py into packages; none of those surfaces has an RF1 pin, so RF-R3's precondition 'No module moves until RF1's characterization tests for the touched surface are green on the pre-move code' is unsatisfiable as written for the two largest move phases.

concerns.recommendation: Either extend RF1's pin list (or make it an explicit per-spec obligation) to cover the surfaces RF4 and RF6 move -- assurance outputs, synth oracle results, agent_cli dispatch, safefs write behavior -- or restate RF1's outcome and RF-R3 to say exactly which surfaces are pinned versus left to inherited controls, so the pin-before-move rule cannot be read as satisfied when it is not.
concerns.title: RF1 pins do not cover the surfaces RF4 and RF6 move, so pin-before-move is unenforceable there

evidence.observation: RF-R7 states 'The runtime and test-acceptance units are still recorded as source-owned (migration/units.json)' and RF0 says 'Record the unit handoff in migration/units.json, and update the test that currently requires every unit to be source-owned.' No migration/units.json exists at the repository root or under this milestone; the ledger is .gnd-planning/milestones/public-launch/migration/units.json, and the guarding assertions are tests/test_public_distribution.py:197 and tests/test_development_scaffold.py:86, which assert every unit of that public-launch ledger is source-owned. RF0 as written therefore rewrites another open milestone's authority ledger and weakens its distribution test before the public-launch Phase 3 acceptance and Phase 4 candidate sign-off that RF-D2 itself makes preconditions.

concerns.recommendation: Name the ledger's real path, state whether the handoff is recorded in the public-launch ledger, a new code-refactoring ledger, or both, and add a recorded coordination step with the public-launch milestone so the ledger flip and the test update cannot land mid-sign-off.
concerns.title: units.json path is wrong and the RF0 handoff edits another open milestone's ledger before its sign-off

evidence.observation: Four pass/fail criteria carry no number of their own: RF5-C3 'cli.py shrinks to at most the line budget the spec declares', RF2-C2 'the duplicate counts for the merged families reach the spec's target', RF3-C2 'the private-import count across the core falls by at least the spec's target', and RF6-C1 'direct reads of fact_types and .get("roles") outside the model package fall to the spec's target'. RF-R9 requires each spec to state budgets, but nothing stops a spec from declaring the current RF0-measured value as the target, which makes the criterion pass vacuously.

concerns.recommendation: Add a plan-level floor or a spec-gate rule that each target must improve on the RF0-measured baseline by a stated delta with recorded justification (e.g. merged duplicate families reach exactly one definition; an order-of-magnitude cli.py ceiling stated now), so a run of the phase can actually fail the criterion.
concerns.title: Four phase criteria defer their thresholds to unwritten specs and can pass vacuously

evidence.observation: Completion predicate 4 requires 'no command handler holds domain logic that api.py or a lane service.py cannot also reach', but RF5's criteria cover only the RF1 pins (RF5-C1), unloaded-module coverage (RF5-C2), the line budget (RF5-C3) and monkeypatch retargeting (RF5-C4); none of them, and no test named anywhere in the plan, checks where handler domain logic lives, so the predicate can be declared met on the strength of a line-count proxy.

concerns.recommendation: Give predicate 4 an enforcing check at RF5 -- for example an import/AST test asserting commands/<group>.py handlers reach domain operations only through api.py or lane service modules, or a spec-level definition of 'domain logic' with a reviewable checklist item -- so satisfying it is demonstrable rather than asserted.
concerns.title: Completion predicate 4 (thin entry points) has no enforcing criterion

evidence.observation: RF4-C3 hardcodes 'the 47 private imports from synth.boundary into synth.mutate are replaced by public oracle imports' and section 9 names 'the 12 files that patch gnd.cli', yet the baseline paragraph says 'No other audit claim was re-proved' -- only the scope numbers were re-measured at 7e08e1e. If RF0 measures a different count, the criterion is either unachievable or vacuously met, and the section 9 starting point silently under- or over-covers.

concerns.recommendation: Phrase count-bearing criteria relative to the RF0-measured value (for example 'every private import from synth.boundary into synth.mutate listed by the RF0 measurement is replaced'), and let the RF0 record re-baseline section 9's starting points.
concerns.title: Unverified audit counts (47, 12) are hardcoded into pass/fail criteria

evidence.location: line 126 (RF0 work items), with lines 5-8, 322 and 327
evidence.observation: RF0 ends 'Settle RF-D2 to RF-D4.', but the status header records 'The owner accepted the RF-D2 and RF-D7 proposals the same day' and the decisions table marks RF-D2 'Accepted by the owner, 2026-10-05' with resolution 'Ruled', while the section 10 preamble still says 'These are proposals awaiting the plan gate. None of them is an approval.' Ruled decisions and undecided ones are mixed in one instruction and one preamble.

concerns.recommendation: Change RF0's item to record the RF-D1/RF-D2/RF-D7 rulings and settle only RF-D3 to RF-D4, and scope the section 10 preamble to the rows that are actually still proposals.
concerns.title: RF0 re-settles RF-D2 although the plan records it as already ruled

response.summary: Digest matched; the plan was read in full and its referenced audit, skills, tests and migration ledger were spot-checked. Pin-before-move (RF-R3), byte contracts (RF-R2), monkeypatch retargeting (RF-R5), source-scan widening (RF-R6), the recorded owner rulings (RF-D1/D2/D7), the RF7 deferral and per-phase stop conditions are present and mostly enforceable. Six concerns, none blocking: RF1's enumerated pins do not cover the surfaces RF4 and RF6 move; the units ledger path is wrong and its RF0 edit touches another open milestone before its sign-off; four pass/fail criteria defer all thresholds to unwritten specs and can pass vacuously; completion predicate 4 has no enforcing check; unverified audit counts are hardcoded as criteria; and RF0 still instructs settling an already-ruled decision.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
Cite one concrete location in the plan for every concern.
Check that every phase criterion is falsifiable: a run of the stated work could fail it.
Check that the behavior-preservation claims are enforceable: pins land before moves, digest-bound bytes and variant encoders, monkeypatch targets and source-scan tests after module moves.
Check sequencing and dependencies, including the recorded owner rulings on execution authority, public-launch sign-off ordering and the RF7 deferral.
Reject unbounded execution: each phase needs measurable budgets and a stop condition.
Flag any plan statement that relies on an unverified audit claim without saying so.
rubric.name: code-refactoring milestone plan review r1
